clue.text: Fool in wet tucking into beer — one shows swallowing motion

indicators.note: tucking into says the whole built piece is pushed inside the word for beer

parts.note: ale is a type of beer

indicators.note: in places the word for fool inside the word for wet

parts.note: damp means slightly wet
a sap is a gullible fool

explanation.surface: Someone foolishly drinking beer in the rain, while another person gulps it down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wet' looks like describing the fool but supplies a word of its own; two nested containers, 'in' then 'tucking into', build the whole.
explanation.definitionFit: The throat bulge visibly bobs up and down whenever a person gulps, so it shows the motion.

clue.text: Anyone can, if provoked, become a pest

indicators.note: provoked suggests stirred up, so the letters of the two words are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Anybody, when riled, can turn into a nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuisance or pest is something that irritates, which is the sense of the noun here.

clue.text: A government about to step down? Excitedly eager

indicators.note: about signals that the word for stepping down is turned round

parts.note: to go is to leave office, to step down

explanation.surface: A government on the verge of resigning, and everyone is eagerly waiting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'step down' here means resign, leave office; 'about' turns that word round.
explanation.definitionFit: Being agog means being keenly expectant, full of excited curiosity.

clue.text: Bad behaviour by member of ensemble cast, not about to be distinctive

parts.note: sin is wrongdoing, bad behaviour

indicators.note: not says the word for about is taken away from the cast member

parts.note: a regular is a recurring member of a show's cast
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: An actor in a group cast misbehaves to stand out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes RE from REGULAR, leaving GULAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Something singular is remarkable or unusual, standing apart from the ordinary.

clue.text: Old man around rescue vessel has warm gear

indicators.note: around has the word for father wrapped about the vessel

parts.note: old man is slang for father, PA
Noah's ark rescued the animals from the flood

explanation.surface: A father on a lifeboat wears warm clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A hooded windproof jacket is a piece of cold-weather clothing.

clue.text: Leased hillside that's a disappointment

parts.note: let means rented out, leased
a down is a rolling hill, as in the South Downs of England

explanation.surface: A rented slope proves to be a disappointment.
explanation.walkthrough: DOWNS are open chalk hills in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A disappointment is an anticlimax, a failure to meet expectations.

clue.text: Warning sailors and reporter about student pop venue

parts.note: cave is Latin for beware, a British schoolboy's warning call
RN is the Royal Navy, hence sailors

indicators.note: about has the word for reporter surrounding the student's letter

parts.note: a cub is a junior reporter
L is a learner, a student, as on L-plates

explanation.surface: Navy men and a journalist warn of something concerning a student music hall.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cavern Club is the Liverpool cellar where the Beatles played; L-plates mark a learner driver in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The Liverpool cellar club was a famous place for live rock and pop acts.

clue.text: Expert in breaking out is to pull out

indicators.note: in places the expert inside the scrambled word
breaking signals that the word out is broken up and rearranged

parts.note: a pro is a professional, an expert

explanation.surface: A professional escapologist is going to tear something out.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'out' is the anagram fodder for 'breaking'; the second belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To uproot is to pull a plant up by the roots, extracting it.

clue.text: Almost all obscene material around hen partying? It's a blast

indicators.note: almost means not quite all of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

indicators.note: around has the word for obscene material wrapped about the rearranged bird

parts.note: porn is obscene material

indicators.note: partying suggests letting loose, so the letters of hen are rearranged

explanation.surface: Smutty items surround a riotous hen party; what a blast!
explanation.walkthrough: A hen party is a British bride's night out before the wedding; 'Almost' trims, 'partying' scrambles and 'around' encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: The long Swiss mountain horn is blown, so the instrument produces a blast of sound.

clue.text: Old plane losing 100 in speed

indicators.note: losing says the Roman numeral is taken away from the plane

parts.note: crate is slang for an old, rickety aircraft
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: An ageing aircraft loses a hundred in speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' removes C from CRATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Rate means pace, as in travelling at a fair rate.

clue.text: The writer recalled introducing horse such as Black Beauty

indicators.note: introducing places the horse inside the reversed pronoun
recalled means called back, so the word for the writer is read backwards

parts.note: the writer is the setter, ME
a pony is a small horse

explanation.surface: An author remembers bringing in a famous horse from a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Black Beauty is both the horse and the title of Anna Sewell's novel; 'recalled' reverses and 'introducing' inserts.
explanation.definitionFit: Black Beauty is the title character whose name gives the novel its title, a namesake character.

clue.text: Cheers fight after turning up for broadcast

indicators.note: after places thanks and fight following the turned word
turning says the word up is turned round

parts.note: ta and cheers both mean thanks in Britain
a bout is a boxing match, a fight

explanation.surface: A boxer's toast to a bout once it shows up on television.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is British informal thanks; 'turning' reverses and 'after' sets the order.
explanation.definitionFit: To put a rumour about is to spread it widely, the verb sense of broadcast.

clue.text: Sailor confused about detective's nonsense

parts.note: a tar is a sailor

indicators.note: about has the word for confused around the detective

parts.note: addle, as in addle-headed, means muddled
DI is a Detective Inspector

explanation.surface: A muddled seaman talks about a policeman's nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: ADDLE survives as an adjective in addle-headed; 'about' wraps it around the detective.
explanation.definitionFit: The old word means a petty fib or pretentious rubbish, so it is idle talk.

clue.text: Observing heartless love

indicators.note: heartless says the central letter is removed

parts.note: love means nil, a score of zero in tennis

explanation.surface: Seeing a love that has no heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes the middle H from NOTHING.
explanation.definitionFit: Noting means taking notice of, remarking upon.

clue.text: Flying expert for clean flying

indicators.note: flying suggests the letters are tossed into the air and land rearranged

explanation.surface: A pilot travels by air to keep things clean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' appears twice: once in the definition, once as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who trains hawks is an authority on birds of prey in flight.

clue.text: Praised in cryptic terms, including male soldiers

indicators.note: including means the coded word takes the male and soldiers inside it

parts.note: coded means written in cryptic terms
men are soldiers, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: Commended in secret language, including male troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link: 'cryptic terms' as a whole means coded; 'including' does the enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: Commended is a synonym meaning praised or spoken well of.

clue.text: More powerful foreigner showing love for one

indicators.note: for marks a swap: the zero shape takes the place of the single letter

parts.note: a stranger is a foreigner, an outsider
A means one, as in a single item
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: An outsider proves mightier, showing love for someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' swaps A for O in STRANGER.
explanation.definitionFit: Stronger is the comparative of strong, having greater power.

clue.text: Nobel winner's line of gold

parts.note: aureate means golden

explanation.surface: A Nobel Prize-winner's lineage is golden.
explanation.walkthrough: 's is 'is' linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A laureate is someone honoured with a prize such as the Nobel.

clue.text: Suspicion of injury? University doctor to show anger

parts.note: MB is a Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree
to rage is to show fury

explanation.surface: A university doctor shows fury at a perceived injury.
explanation.definitionFit: The original sense is resentment at a suspected slight, hence taking offence.

clue.text: Entertained our group, diving into a sea

indicators.note: diving into says our group goes inside the sea

parts.note: Med is the Mediterranean Sea
us means our group

explanation.surface: Our gang are having fun plunging into a sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The Med is the usual shortening of the Mediterranean; 'diving into' does the inserting.
explanation.definitionFit: Amused means diverted or delighted, kept entertained.

clue.text: Shrill sound from endless wind rounding far end of Naze

indicators.note: rounding means the shortened wind goes around the picked letter
endless means the last letter of the wind is cut off

parts.note: a squall is a sudden gust of wind

indicators.note: far end of picks the last letter of the place name

explanation.surface: A gusty wind whistles round The Naze, a headland in Essex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts SQUALL to SQUAL, and 'rounding' puts E, the last letter of Naze, inside it. The Naze is an Essex headland.
explanation.definitionFit: A squeal is a high-pitched cry.

clue.text: Major issue taking several years to produce

definitions.text: Major issue taking several years to produce

parts.words: Major issue taking several years to produce
parts.note: issue means offspring, so a large crop of children born across several years, not a big problem slow to solve

explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' looks like a problem but means children; 'major' means great in number.
explanation.definitionFit: The post-war surge in births was a great increase in children over several years.

clue.text: Partner inclined to raise objections?

explanation.walkthrough: BUTTY is Welsh and northern English slang for a friend; the second reading treats it as 'given to buts'.
explanation.definitionFit: Butty is dialect for a mate or workmate; whimsically it also describes someone always saying 'but'.

clue.text: Productive City surrounded by source of money

indicators.note: surrounded by puts the City's letters inside the source of money

parts.note: a fund is a pool of money
EC is the postcode of the City of London

explanation.surface: The financial district enclosed by a money supply is fruitful.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is the postcode area of the City of London, its financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: Fecund means fertile, highly fruitful.

clue.text: Long line coming out of station

indicators.note: coming out of says the line leaves the station

parts.note: a power station is a plant

explanation.surface: A long train line departs from a station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming out of' removes L from PLANT.
explanation.definitionFit: To pant for something is to long or yearn for it.

clue.text: No opening to begin cutting flan

indicators.note: no opening means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: to start is to begin

explanation.surface: No way in to start slicing the flan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No opening' removes S from START. 'cutting' also means TART (sharp), a bonus definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tart is an open pastry case with a filling, like a flan.

clue.text: Safety measure: recalled medicine after receiving a protest

indicators.note: receiving means the reversed medicine takes a inside it
recalled means the medicine is read backwards

parts.note: a drug is a medicine
to rail is to protest angrily

explanation.surface: A medicine is recalled after a protest about safety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns DRUG to GURD; 'receiving' puts A inside, giving GUARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrier rail is fitted to stop falls, a safety device.

clue.text: How "the dead dry" may be represented?

definitions.text: How "the dead dry" may be represented?

indicators.note: represented here means presented again in a new arrangement, so the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A question on how to describe the dried-out remains of the dead.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters of the quoted phrase describe the dead dry: mummified, with water removed.
explanation.definitionFit: The dead being dry means they have lost all water, the state described.
